practices.claim: Give Claude a runnable check (tests, build, linter) and have it iterate until the check passes.
practices.check: Read the share of editing sessions that ran a test/build/lint/typecheck after the last edit. A low share is a gap only for sessions where a check existed; do not call doc-only or config edits a miss.
practices.notes: Docs: 'the difference between a session you watch and one you walk away from' (date shown is the fetch date; docs are undated). Anthropic's June 2026 expertise study links expertise to 'verified success', but the link is correlational and partly circular.

practices.claim: Have Claude show command output as evidence rather than just claiming it worked.
practices.check: No metric checks this; a sample reader can look at whether final messages quote check output.
practices.notes: Docs advice, no data.

practices.claim: Tell Claude in the prompt or CLAUDE.md to verify its own work before finishing.
practices.check: Do not recommend adding verification boilerplate to a current-model setup; see the replacing entry.
practices.notes: Useful advice on earlier models; the prompting docs now warn it over-triggers on Opus 5.

practices.claim: On Opus 5, remove carried-over 'verify your work' instructions; they cause over-verification (extra tokens and latency).
practices.check: A hard check (test, hook) is still good; look for the same check re-run several times with no edit between, not for a low verification rate. Never read few verify phrases in prompts as a gap.
practices.notes: Docs: 'verification instructions carried over… can cause over-verification, adding tokens and latency… remove these instructions'. Thariq Shihipar, 2026-09-29 (x.com/trq212/status/2104983034152063339): 'Smart models need less verification which makes them pareto dominant.'

practices.claim: Use plan mode (explore, plan, then code) for multi-file or uncertain work; skip it if you could describe the diff in one sentence.
practices.check: Compare plan-mode use against diff size only if the data allows it. Zero plan-mode use is not a gap on current models: the auto-mode posts argue plan mode is no longer needed.
practices.notes: Docs say plan mode 'adds overhead' for small changes. Conflicts with the auto-mode advice below. Expertise study: users make about 70% of planning decisions, correlated with success (correlational).

practices.claim: Start most sessions in plan mode.
practices.check: Do not flag low plan-mode use as a gap. Boris and Thariq have since moved away from it.
practices.notes: Source is secondary (paddo.dev); x.com was not fetched directly for this post. Kept because the later first-hand posts reverse it.

practices.claim: Use auto mode instead of plan mode; current models do not need plan mode.
practices.check: Read permission-mode mix and plan-mode count as description, not grade. Heavy manual approval with no auto mode is the signal worth mentioning, not plan-mode absence.
practices.notes: Boris 2026-05-22: 'my #1 tip is: use auto mode'. Boris 2026-06-08 (status/2064034799711588805) gives 'why I use auto mode instead of plan mode'. Thariq 2026-09-23 (x.com/trq212/status/2102813194196758746): 'thinking of killing plan mode… I don't think the models need plan mode anymore'. Opinion, no data.

practices.claim: Write prompts that name files, constraints, existing patterns, the symptom and what 'fixed' looks like.
practices.check: A high correction rate may reflect vague prompts, but it also reflects hard tasks and model changes; use samples to judge, never the rate alone.
practices.notes: Costs doc: vague requests 'trigger broad scanning'. Economic Index (2026-01-15) shows prompt and response sophistication correlate; no causal claim.

practices.claim: Keep CLAUDE.md under about 200 lines and move occasional workflows into skills.
practices.check: Compare loaded lines against 200. A long file is a cost and instruction-following risk, not proof of a problem; check for rules Claude then ignored.
practices.notes: Docs: 'Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!'

practices.claim: Repository context files raised inference cost by over 20% and gave little or no success gain in a benchmark.
practices.check: Supports pruning, but the data is SWE-bench-style tasks on Sonnet 4.5-era models. Do not apply the 20% figure to this user's own sessions.
practices.notes: Developer-written files added about 4% success on average; for Claude Code with Sonnet 4.5 no gain on the page fetch. Title: Evaluating AGENTS.md.

practices.claim: After each correction, tell Claude to update CLAUDE.md so it does not repeat the mistake, and prune it ruthlessly.
practices.check: Growth alone is not a gap. Look at whether the file grows without pruning while repeat corrections persist.
practices.notes: Boris: 'Ruthlessly edit your CLAUDE.md over time. Keep iterating until Claude's mistake rate measurably drops.' Pulls against the short-file advice and the AGENTS.md data, but his own post also says to prune.

practices.claim: Use /clear between unrelated tasks instead of one long kitchen-sink session.
practices.check: Compare /clear counts and sessions with 2+ compactions. Long sessions on one topic are fine; do not count them as a gap.
practices.notes: Costs doc calls clearing between tasks and matching the model to the job the highest-impact habits. Docs also say 'Sometimes you should let context accumulate'.

practices.claim: Models get less reliable as the input grows, even on simple tasks.
practices.check: Use only as background for long sessions. It was measured on 18 models in isolated tasks, not on agentic Claude Code sessions or current models.
practices.notes: Anthropic's context engineering post (2025-09-29) cites it.

practices.claim: After two failed corrections on the same issue, /clear and re-prompt instead of correcting a third time.
practices.check: Count sessions with 2+ consecutive corrections and read samples to see whether it was the same issue. A streak is not always a failure: the task may simply be iterative.
practices.notes: Docs: 'A clean session with a better prompt almost always outperforms a long session with accumulated corrections'. No data.

practices.claim: Interrupt (Esc) or /rewind early instead of letting a bad trajectory run.
practices.check: Read interrupts and rewinds per session. Zero interrupts is not a gap if corrections are rare.
practices.notes: Descriptive data: users under 50 sessions interrupt in about 5% of turns, 750+ sessions about 9%. The paper says no oversight style is universally superior.

practices.claim: Use subagents for investigation and verbose operations so the main context gets only a short summary.
practices.check: Compare agent calls and sizes against main-context compactions. More subagents is not better; see the cost and over-spawn entries.
practices.notes: Context engineering post: subagent summaries are 'often 1,000-2,000 tokens'.

practices.claim: Multi-agent runs use far more tokens (about 15x a chat) and help coding less than research.
practices.check: Use cost.total split main vs subagents and agents.size. The 90.2% gain was on research evals, so do not claim it applies to coding.
practices.notes: 'multi-agent systems use about 15× more tokens than chats'. Costs doc: agent teams use about 7x more tokens in plan mode.

practices.claim: On Opus 4.6 and later, avoid spawning subagents for work a direct grep or read would do faster.
practices.check: Read agent calls per week and sampled prompts. A high count is a gap only if the tasks were trivial.
practices.notes: Prompting docs warn these models over-use subagents.

practices.claim: Set a model on subagent calls (for example haiku for simple ones) instead of inheriting the parent's.
practices.check: Read the explicit rate with agents.by_model. A low rate costs money only when the parent is an expensive model and the tasks are simple; inheriting is fine for hard work.
practices.notes: Costs doc recommends model: haiku for simple subagents.

practices.claim: Run several sessions in parallel, using worktrees to keep them apart.
practices.check: Worktree use and overlapping sessions show the habit. They do not show it paid off.
practices.notes: METR transcripts of 7 staff: more concurrent agents went with higher estimated time savings, but n=7 and METR calls it a soft upper bound. Boris's 'single biggest productivity unlock' posts are secondary and left out.

practices.claim: Use Sonnet for most coding and Opus for hard reasoning; unexpectedly high spend usually traces to Opus left as default.
practices.check: Report model mix and cost by model. Do not call heavy Opus use wrong: Boris's Jan 2026 view (secondary, not fetched first-hand) was Opus with thinking for everything, and neither side shows data.
practices.notes: Costs doc: 'Sonnet handles most coding tasks well and costs less than Opus.'

practices.claim: Keep effort at a high setting for non-trivial coding.
practices.check: The effort setting is not in the transcripts reliably; use /insights or ask the user. Do not conclude anything from absence.
practices.notes: Default change high to medium on 2026-03-04 gave 'slightly lower intelligence with significantly less latency' on internal evals; reverted 2026-04-07. Defaults have changed, so any advice tied to one is dated.

practices.claim: Do not switch model, effort, or the tool set mid-session; hand off to another model via a subagent.
practices.check: Read the model_change row of cost.cache.by_cause. Effort switches no longer break the cache on Opus/Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 (API/subscription), so check the model before blaming the user.
practices.notes: Follows from pricing, not a behavioural finding. Thariq, 2026-04-30 (Prompt caching is everything): switching Opus to Haiku after 100k tokens costs more than staying.

practices.claim: Do not idle past the cache TTL mid-task; a cold turn costs 12.5x to 20x a warm one.
practices.check: Read the idle_over_ttl row, using meta.billing.main_cache_ttl for the right TTL. Breaks after a real task end are normal; only mid-task gaps count.
practices.notes: Multipliers: read 0.1x, 5m write 1.25x, 1h write 2x. Main-thread TTL is 1h on a subscription within plan usage, 5m otherwise; subagents 5m by default. Opus 5.5 reads at 0.05x and Fable 5.1 at 0.025x, so the cold/warm ratio is larger there.

practices.claim: Use /rewind rather than /compact to abandon a path; compact at natural breaks, not mid-task or after the cache expires.
practices.check: Read the compaction row and /rewind use in practices.usage. A compaction that was needed to continue is not waste.
practices.notes: /compact on a cold cache 'reprocesses the full history as uncached input'; /rewind keeps an already-cached prefix.

practices.claim: A subagent's first request does not read the parent's cache, and subagents default to a 5-minute TTL.
practices.check: Read subagent_start_pct and what_if.subagent_ttl_1h. It is structural, so many small subagents cost more than a few large ones; do not call it a user error.
practices.notes: A fork does read the parent's cache.

practices.claim: Use hooks for rules that must always hold and to pre-filter large output; CLAUDE.md is only advisory.
practices.check: Hook config is not in transcripts. Oversized tool results or a repeated violation of a CLAUDE.md rule are indirect hints only.
practices.notes: Docs: hooks are 'deterministic', CLAUDE.md 'advisory'. The tens-of-thousands-to-hundreds token saving is an illustration, not a measurement.

practices.claim: Prefer CLI tools such as gh to MCP servers and disable unused MCP servers.
practices.check: MCP tools are now deferred by default, so the cost gap is smaller. Do not flag MCP use without evidence of definition-token cost.
practices.notes: Costs doc and best-practices call CLI the most context-efficient option; partly stale.

practices.claim: Pre-approve safe commands or use auto mode instead of clicking through prompts.
practices.check: Read permission-mode mix. Heavy manual prompting is a time cost, but auto mode is 'not a drop-in replacement for careful human review on high-stakes infrastructure'.
practices.notes: Users approve 93% of prompts; classifier has 0.4% false positives and 17% false negatives on real overeager actions.

practices.claim: People misjudge their own AI productivity, so do not trust a self-reported or transcript-derived time saving.
practices.check: Never report hours saved. Report process signals only.
practices.notes: RCT, 16 developers: forecast 24% faster, believed 20% faster, measured 19% slower (CI +2% to +39%). Claude 3.x era; METR's 2026 re-runs point toward speedup but call the signal unreliable.

practices.claim: More code or merged PRs does not mean better outcomes; complexity and warnings can rise with it.
practices.check: Do not praise lines written or sessions run. Prefer rework signals.
practices.notes: Found a transient velocity gain with a persistent rise in static-analysis warnings and complexity; Cursor, not Claude Code.

practices.claim: Avoid CRITICAL/MUST shouting in prompts and CLAUDE.md; use emphasis on one line at most.
practices.check: Count of emphasis words in CLAUDE.md is a hint only; a transcript cannot show over-triggering.
practices.notes: Docs: dial back aggressive language, it 'may now overtrigger'.
